Increased lacrimation (tear production) was reported in 1% of patients. 3. Some patients may experience symptomatic orthostatic hypotension, characterized by an inability to stand without support after lying down for 5 minutes. Patients who feel dizziness or lightheadedness after administration should lie down until symptoms resolve. 4. Patients with onchocerciasis who are also infected with Loa loa may develop serious or even fatal encephalopathy following treatment. Moxidectin has not been studied in patients co-infected with Loa loa. 5. Before initiating treatment, patients who require therapy and have been exposed to Loa loa-endemic areas are recommended to undergo diagnostic screening for loiasis. 6. Patients with hyper-reactive onchodermatitis (sowda) may have a higher likelihood of experiencing severe edema and worsening of onchodermatitis after moxidectin treatment. These symptoms should be managed with symptomatic treatment in affected patients. 7. Limited data on the use of moxidectin in pregnant women are insufficient to determine whether there is an associated risk of major birth defects or miscarriage. 8. Moxidectin has been detected in the milk of lactating women following a single dose. However, there is no data on the effects of moxidectin on breastfed infants or milk production. 9. In a preand postnatal study conducted in rats, oral administration of moxidectin at a dose less than twice the recommended human dose (based on body surface area comparison) during the lactation period resulted in adverse clinical signs, weight loss, and increased mortality in rat pups. This suggests that moxidectin in lactation milk was responsible for these adverse effects. 10. Due to the serious findings from the rat preand postnatal study, including weight loss and death, women are advised not to breastfeed during treatment and for 7 days after treatment. 11. Moxidectin is generally considered acceptable for use. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. 12. The mechanism of action of moxidectin against Onchocerca volvulus is not fully understood. 13. Moxidectin is active against the microfilariae of Onchocerca volvulus. 14. The drug is excreted primarily via feces, with 2% excreted unchanged. 15. Moxidectin can be administered with or without food as a single dose. 16. Tablets should be stored at temperatures below 30°C (86°F) and protected from light. Once the container is opened, the full contents should be used within 24 hours, and any unused content should be discarded. 17.
